comments.text:
What if the Dutch had gotten Louisiana instead of the French?

They wouldn’t have founded a city on a natural levee in a swamp and then spent centuries fighting the water. They would have built dike rings, windmills, later steam and electric pumps, and active water-level management so the land didn’t compact and sink as fast. That’s the same reason Amsterdam is considered viable long-term while New Orleans is often called doomed — not because the geography is that different, but because of centuries of systematic water engineering.New Orleans would probably have a Dutch name (Nieuw-Oranje, Willemstad, Nieuw-Rotterdam) and look more like Rotterdam: canals as a feature, not just hidden drainage ditches behind floodwalls. The Mississippi would still be a monster compared to the Rhine, and hurricanes would still be a problem the Netherlands never had to face. But the fundamental mistake — draining wetlands, letting the city become a bowl, and starving the coast of sediment — would likely have been avoided or at least managed much earlier.Commercially it could have been even stronger. The Dutch were traders first. Control of the Mississippi mouth plus that mindset might have made it the Rotterdam of North America.Culturally it would be very different: less French/Creole/Cajun, more Protestant trading-port mixed with African and later American influences. Slavery would still have been there (the WIC was deep in that business), so that part of the history wouldn’t suddenly become pretty.The irony is that after Katrina, Louisiana actually brought in Dutch engineers. In this timeline they would have been there 250 years earlier. Louisiana might still be struggling with the river and the Gulf, but it probably wouldn’t be the cautionary tale it is today.
